lede: The biggest thing on the public calendar this week is a joint session in Ouray where the City Council and County Commissioners will sit down together — with public comment open at 5:00 PM — to work through a draft intergovernmental agreement that would hand full law enforcement for the City of Ouray to the County Sheriff starting January 1, 2027. Closer to home, Telluride Town Council meets Tuesday with a public hearing on a vesting-period extension and a work session on Flock Safety license plate reader cameras — a conversation about surveillance technology that rarely stays quiet. San Miguel County's Planning Commission spends Thursday on an Affordable Housing Code Update in a joint session with the BOCC, which is about as consequential as land-use work gets right now.
